text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Shares in Australia's mining giants took another sharp fall yesterday, with BHP Ltd, CRA Ltd, WMC Ltd and MIM Holdings Ltd losing a combined A$4.6 billion in market value this month alone. The sell-off in the resources sector has been sparked by the slump in the copper price, significant downgradings in earnings forecasts and forecasts of worldwide economic growth which have failed to materialise. Page 1.

The BHP board can expect a fiery annual meeting today as shareholders air their views over the miner's A$3.2 billion purchase of the loss-making Magma Copper. However, even more of a problem for BHP, is its negative cash flow in three of the past five years which has thumped the company's share price down from A$20 in May to a low of A$15.75 yesterday. Page 1.

Delivering the third annual Australia Lecture in Jakarta, new Austrade chairman Alan Jackson announced plans to develop a strong export culture through awards, conferences and promotion and forecast a substantial increase in Indonesian investment in Australia across a wide range of industries. Page 2.

A survey sponsored by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and accounting firm KPMG, shows that the recent interest rate cut and the Budget had helped boost confidence in the construction and utilities sector of the economy, as well as retailing, making the business sector keen for another cut in interest rates. However, directors in the transport, communications, mining and agriculture sectors have become less confident about the future for their companies. Page 3.

News Ltd chairman and chief executive officer Ken Cowley will move to a more strategic role to make way for Lachlan Murdoch to step in as managing director, a step closer to succeeding his father, Rupert Murdoch, as chief executive of the family-controled communications company News Corp. Cowley is also preparing to step down as executive chairman of the Ansett group after a four-year rule. Page 21.

Santos Ltd has bought the bulk of MIM Holdings Ltd's oil and gas acreage for A$45.1 million, delivering Santos exploration potential in New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the Carnarvon Basin in offshore Western Australia and oil production from PNG's South-East Gobe filed. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The stock market, led by another fall in BHP shares, plummeted and currency markets were paralysed yesterday ahead of tonight's crucial meeting of the United States Federal Reserve to consider interest rate policy, with analysts warning any rise in US interest rates could cause a fall in the Australian dollar. Page 19.

BHP chairman Brian Loton will today, possibly for the last time, publicly defend the group from its critics at the annual meeting. Criticisms are expected over BHP's decision to spend A$3.2 billion on an American acquisition, Magma Copper Co, which has fuelled doubts over the company's direction. Page 19.

Financial services giant Colonial Mutual Group accelerated its push into banking yesterday by opening the first Colonial State Bank, previously State Bank of New South Wales, at the Miranda shopping centre in Sydney and announcing plans to expand the renamed banking arm into Western Australia and South Australia. Page 19.

Lachlan Murdoch, the son of News Corp chief executive and chairman Rupert Murdoch, has recieved his most significant promotion since arriving in Australia in 1994 by being appointed as managing director of News Limited, the Australian arm of The News Corpration Ltd. Page 19.

In a new Treasury-initiated revenue blitz, to be carried out jointly by the Australian Taxation Office and the Industry Research and Development Board, the ATO is planning a retrospective audit program of companies which have used the research and developent tax concession. Page 21.

In the third aggressive takeover play for an Australian petroleum producer in the past nine months, UK-based Premier Oil Plc yesterday launched a surprise 70 cents-a-share, A$91.9 million bid for Discovery Petroleum NL , as part of Premier's strategic expasion into the Australian and Asian energy markets. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a move that positions Lachlan Murdoch, the 29-year-old son of media magnate Rupert Murdoch, as one of the youngest, most powerful and best paid media executives in Australia, it was announced yesterday Lachlan was appointed as managing director of New Ltd, News Corporation's Australian operations. Page 1.

Ahead of a major interstate push involving establishing physical branches and electronic delivery channels, Colonial Mutual yesterday revealed its plans for the State Bank of New South Wales - a restructure of the branch network and a name change, to Colonial State. Page 21.

Leading broker JB Were's analysis of the 1995-96 profit reporting season has confirmed that Australia's listed companies are forecast to suffer a further profit slump in the current half-year. Were has predicted a decline of four to five per cent in net profits in the December half. Page 21.

The just completed 1996 profit reporting season has shown that the blue chips - companies such as Pacific Dunlop, Amcor and Boral which have offered the conservative investor strong management, a long track record and a competitive dividend yield - are facing tough competition and are fighting to find fresh growth. Page 21.

As part of its business expansion throughout Australia and in international markets, Australia's largest cotton producer, Colly Cotton, issued its float prospectus yesterday and is seeking A$107 million through a public listing. Colly forecasts 1996-97 net earnings of A$21.4 million, based on an expected upturn in the agricultural sector and expansion of its irrigated farmlands. Page 23.

After offloading its 25 per cent stake in Optus Communications later this year, stockbroking analysts believe Mayne Nickless shares will trade at a 10 per cent premium to the industrial market. It is tipped that the premium will be justified by Mayne's pln to position itself as the country's largest private health care company. Page 23.
THE AGE

Australia's biggest cotton producer, Colly Cotton, yesterday tapped the sharemarket for more than A$100 million in capital, planning to use the raising for expansion and moves into international markets. The float will take to more than A$400 million the amount raised this financial year. Page C1.

BHP's 13 directors are expected to hear a list of grievances from shareholders at the annual meeting in Sydney today, starting with BHP's plunging share price, which dropped another 22 cents to a two-year low of A$15.82 yesterday. Also sure to figure among shareholders' concerns is the first-quarter profits slump in steel and minerals and the ever-growing boardroom payroll. Page C1.

Lachlan Murdoch, the son of media mogul Rupert Murdoch, was appointed managing director of News Ltd yesterday, with Ken Cowley continuing as executive chairman, a News Corp director and a member of News' international executive committee. Page C1.

According to a survey of company directors by the Australian Institute of Company Directors and accounting firm KPMG, confidence in the economy over the next 12 months had risen marginally from 67 per cent in the June quarter to 70 per cent in September. age C1.

Following the A$45.1 million sale of most of its oil and gas business to Santos yesterday, MIM Holdings took another step back to its core activities. MIM chief executive Nick Stump said the proceeds would go towards expanding the Mount Isa copper operatons, the A$350 million Ernest Henry gold/copper mine and the El Alumbera copper project in Argentina. Page C3.

Telstra seems to be appearing everywhere with co-branding deals and strategies to leverage its way into the payments system. First was ANZ's Telstra Visa card, and now Telstra wants to get in on the action of stored-value cards - the so-called smart card in Australia. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
